pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: You're modeling a contact with a name, an age, and an email. Why is a struct the right tool rather than a map or three parallel slices?
expected_points: a struct groups values of different types into one value with named fields
map values all share one type, so mixed data doesn't fit
parallel slices drift apart; a struct keeps one thing's parts together

questions.prompt: Show the two ways to write a Contact literal. Why do we insist on the field-named form?
expected_points: field-named: Contact{Name: ..., Age: ...}; positional: Contact{...} with values in field order
positional literals silently swap same-typed fields if the struct is reordered
adding a field breaks every positional literal; named ones keep compiling
named fields document the code; omitted fields get zero values

questions.prompt: Contact embeds Person. What does 'promotion' let you write, and how would it differ if Person were a named field like `P Person`?
expected_points: embedding: field access shortens to c.Name, which is the same field as c.Person.Name
a named field requires the full path (c.P.Name); nothing is promoted
there is still a real field named Person, and literals must nest Person: Person{...}
it is composition, not inheritance

questions.prompt: When does `==` work on two struct values, and when does it refuse to compile? What did that mean for Contact vs Group in the exercise?
expected_points: == compares field by field and needs every field to be comparable
slices and maps are not comparable, so one such field makes struct == a compile error
Contact (strings, int) compared with one ==; Group's []string forced a manual field-by-field comparison
the failure is at compile time, not runtime

questions.prompt: Rename assigns to c.Name and returns c. Why doesn't the caller's contact change, and why must Rename return the contact?
expected_points: structs are values: the parameter is a copy of the caller's struct
mutating the copy is invisible to the caller
returning the changed copy hands the new value back; the caller keeps it by assignment

questions.prompt: Could you build a map[Person]string? A map[Group]string? Connect your answer to struct comparison.
expected_points: map keys must be comparable
Person has only comparable fields, so it can be a key
Group contains a slice, so it is not comparable and cannot be a key
